analytic.title: Fault-Tolerant Scheduling in Hierarchical Real-Time Scheduling Framework

div.p: As real-time systems become complex and require high-performance, Hierarchical Real-Time Scheduling Framework (HRTSF) has been investigated to schedule real-time tasks to meet their deadlines by sharing resources hierarchically under various scheduling algorithms. In this paper, we focus on fault-tolerant scheduling in the hierarchical real-time scheduling framework. Thus, we introduce a new component interface model which provides abstract information about a component's fault-tolerant real-time requirement. The upper-layer component can use the interface model to share its resource with consideration of both real-time and fault-tolerance. We also provide the schedulability analysis of Rate Monotonic (RM) algorithm under the proposed framework and apply it to a case study of designing avionics software as an example of Cyber Physical Systems (CPS).

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: As real-time systems become complex and require highperformance, Hierarchical Real-Time Scheduling Framework (HRTSF) has been investigated to schedule real-time tasks to meet their deadlines by sharing resources hierarchically under various scheduling algorithms. In the hierarchical realtime scheduling framework, a system is usually composed of multiple levels of components, where independent components in a level share a computational resource allocated from a parent component to its child components.

Many frameworks [1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [7] have been proposed for modeling hierarchical real-time scheduling framework. In [1], a hierarchical real-time virtual resource model that permits resource partitioning to be extended to multiple levels is introduced. Through this model, partitions on each level are scheduled as if they had access to a dedicated resource and there is minimal interference between neighboring partition levels.

In [2], [5], a periodic resource model is proposed for a compositional hierarchical scheduling framework. The periodic resource model describes the behavior of a periodic resource, so that a periodic resource Γ(Π, Θ) guarantees to supply Θ computational time units to a component per each resource period Π. Shin and Lee [4] extended this framework to support the bounded-delay task model and developed an exact schedulability condition. In [3], a framework for compositional and hierarchical real-time scheduling is proposed to permit resource partitioning to be extended to multiple levels and handle a wider range of scheduling algorithms and task models.

Many studies have been done on fault-tolerant real-time systems using time redundancy [9], [10], [11], [12]. In [10], single or multiple faults are recovered by re-executing faulty tasks based on RM (Rate-Monotonic) algorithm. In [11], the checkpointing scheme is used for tolerating faults so that a faulty task rolls back to the recent checkpointing status. In [13], they provided exact feasibility tests for any fixed-priority preemptive scheduling algorithm based on re-execution, forward error recovery, and checkpointing recovery schemes.

As multiprocessor and multicore technologies have been developed, transient faults are recovered both in temporally and spatially using multiple processors [19], [20], [18]. Backup tasks can be active if they are executed concurrently with their primary tasks. Otherwise, they are called passive backup tasks and just ready for execution in case of faults in primary tasks. In [20], rate-monotonic first-fit assignment algorithm is used to allocate backup tasks in different processors. In [21], they evaluate various partitioning schemes for fault-tolerant realtime scheduling in multiprocessors. In [22], they enhance the performance by terminating the execution of active backup tasks when their primary tasks are finished successfully. In [24], they apply hierarchical real-time techniques to support fault-tolerance in multicore real-time embedded systems.

As hierarchical real-time scheduling framework takes an important role in safety-critical real-time systems, such as aircraft and automobile systems, research on fault-tolerant scheduling in the framework should be solved. For example, modern avionics software architectures are based on IMA (Integrated Modular Avionics) architecture where partitions are independent components separated each other temporally and spatially. Temporal partitioning assures that the service received from shared resources in one partition cannot be affected by other partitions. ARINC specification 653-2 specifies software interface in avionics based on IMA [17]. In order to support high dependability of such systems, research on faulttolerant scheduling in the framework is required.

Thus, this paper focuses on how to tolerating faults in hierarchical real-time framework. The main contributions of this paper include: (i) introducing a new hierarchical real-time scheduling framework for fault-tolerance; and (ii) providing scheduling analysis of fault-tolerant rate monotonic scheduling in a periodic resource model.

The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section II defines the system model including hierarchical real-time scheduling framework and fault model. In Section III, we introduce the proposed fault-tolerant framework and provide the schedulability analysis of fault-tolerant rate monotonic algorithm. Section IV analyzes a case study of fault-tolerant partitioning of major software in avionics mission computers. We conclude the paper with a summary and the future work in Section V.

div.head: II. SYSTEM MODEL A. Hierarchical Real-Time Scheduling Framework
div.p: A Hierarchical Real-Time Scheduling Framework (HRTSF) is a scheduling framework to support real-time systems which are composed of multiple levels of real-time components with a hierarchy. Multiple components in each level share a computational resource allocated from their parent component. Thus, the basic unit of the HRTSF is a component which is defined by (W, R, A) as follows.

• W : workload or a set of tasks in a component • R: resource model supported from a upper level • A: scheduling algorithm of W for a given resource model R A workload set W is composed of periodic real-time tasks on a single processor. Each task τ i is defined by (p i , e i ), so that a task τ i releases a job of e i execution time per every p i time units. We also assume that the deadline of τ i equals to p i .

A resource model R specifies the amount of resource allocated from a parent or upper-layer component. In this paper, we use the periodic resource model Γ(Π, Θ) [4], [5], where Π is the resource supply period and Θ is the resource supply time per period. A component with the resource model Γ(Π, Θ) is guaranteed to be supplied with Θ resource time every Π time units from its upper-layer component.

In contrast to the resource model, the interface model takes the role of abstracting a component with collective real-time Fig. 1. An exmaple of HRTSF resource requirements. In the HRTSF, the interface model I is defined by (P, E), where P is period and E is resource supply time. If the resource with the amount of E is supported per the period P from upper level, then the feasibility condition for a component is guaranteed.

For example, Figure 1 shows an example of the hierarchical real-time scheduling framework. The component C 1 has two periodic real-time tasks and scheduled by Earliest Deadline First (EDF). The interface I 1 is the real-time component interface by merging those two requirements as a single realtime requirement. Similarly, C 2 contains two tasks scheduled by Rate Monotonic (RM) and provides the interface model I 2 .

To the higher level component C 0 , the two component abstraction models, I 1 and I 2 are considered as two real-time periodic tasks. Therefore, the component considers two subcomponents as sub-tasks with periodic real-time requirements based on their interface models, which makes it easier to compose multi-layer real-time systems. Upon the compositional scheduling policy of C 0 , two resource models R 1 and R 2 are assigned to components C 1 and C 2 respectively in order to meet their real-time requirements.

div.head: B. Fault Model
div.p: In this paper, we consider transient faults in the system. Only the single task which is in the execution at the time of fault occurrence is affected by the fault. When a task fault is detected, it is recovered by the task's recovery scheme, such as re-execution, forward recovery, or checkpointing. Thus, a periodic task τ i defines its own recovery scheme and its backup task is denoted by β i . The backup task's execution time, denoted by b i , is assumed to be less than or equal to the primary task's execution time (0 ≤ b i ≤ e i ). The backup execution time varies according to recovery scheme as follows.

• b i = e i : the re-execution recovery scheme • 0 < b i < e i : the forward error recovery scheme, such as exception handler • b i = 0: ignoring the task fault The task fault is assumed to be detected at the end of the task execution. In case of a fault occurrence in τ i , its backup task β i should be finished by the task deadline. Thus, a periodic job of task τ i should be finished by (p ib i ) time units in order to make slack time for its backup task. A fault in the system is assumed to occur only once in T F time units, which is considered as Mean-Time-To-Failure (MTTF).

div.head: III. FAULT-TOLERANT SCHEDULING IN HRTSF A. The Proposed Scheduling Framework
div.p: In this subsection, we define a new scheduling framework for fault-tolerant hierarchical real-time scheduling systems. Figure 2 shows an example of the proposed framework. Each component contains a fault manager to detect and handle faults in the component. The scheduling algorithm should be able to handle faults, such as FT-RM or FT-EDF.

In addition, a new interface model is used for abstracting the component requirement, which is defined by (P, E, B, M ). P and E are the same as in the previous interface model in [4], In the proposed framework, many interesting problems are to be solved. The followings are such problems.

• Schedulability analysis: For a given periodic resource model Γ(Π, Θ), the feasibility of a component task set should be analyzed in order to guarantee real-time requirements of tasks with consideration of faults. • Defining an optimal periodic resource model: The upperlayer component requires an optimal resource sharing scheme which guarantees all real-time requirements of its sub-components.

• Deriving an interface model: In order to abstract a component as a single task, a method to derive an optimal interface model is required. In this paper, we focus on the schedulability analysis of FT-RM scheduling algorithm for a given periodic resource model. Based on the analysis, other problems can be solved.

div.head: B. Fault-Tolerant RM in Periodic Resource Model
div.p: The fault-tolerant RM scheduling algorithm is based on RM, so that shorter-period tasks have higher priorities than longerperiod ones. Without loss of generality, we assume that tasks are sorted in non-decreasing order of their periods, that is, p i ≤ p i+1 . When a task τ i detects a fault at the end of its execution, its backup task β i is released. The new backup task β i has the same priority as the primary task and scheduled by RM algorithm.

div.head: IV. CASE STUDY
div.p: In this section, we apply the proposed fault-tolerant scheduling framework to avionics softwares as an example of Cyber Physical Systems (CPS). A Mission Computer (MC) in an aircraft controls and communicates with different kinds of sensors including radar, Line Replacement Units (LRUs), and other physical systems such as missiles and bombs on the aircraft. Their timely responses from and to a MC are very critical preserving their accuracy even in some presence of faults.

We use the proposed scheduling framework to partitioning of OFPs (Operational Flight Programs) in avionics mission computers. Although mission computers in avionics consist of many software, we select ten major programs in general mission computers [23]. Table I shows general OFPs in mission computers and their characteristics. In order to apply the proposed framework to partitioning and scheduling OFPs, we modified data in Table I based on the following assumptions. The modified data of components and tasks are shown in Table II.

• The execution time information of Table I is in 1990s [23]. As CPUs in modern avionics have better performance, the execution time of each task is assumed to be half of that in Table I for the simplicity. • For the ease of schedulability analysis, all the periods are reduced to the least 10 × 2 k less than those in Table I. • The execution time of each backup task is based on its criticality. The backup tasks of level Critical use reexecution policy, so that they have the same execution times as the primary tasks. For tasks with level Essential, forward error recovery schemes are used and backup execution times are assumed to be half of execution times of their primary tasks. And, there is no recovery scheme for tasks with level Background. • We classified ten functions into three groups in which they have similar functions.

We fix the resource period Π as 5 msec and define 1.5 msec as the resource supply time for each component. Thus, the periodic resource models of three components are given by Γ 1 = Γ 2 = Γ 3 = (5, 1.5). Figure 5 shows all resource demand functions of ten tasks and supply bound functions of three resource models. As shown in Figure 5, each task is schedulable since there exists t ≤ p i such that dbf(FT-RM, t, i) ≤ sbf Γ (t) for each task τ i . Therefore, partitioning of three components in Table II with periodic resource supply of Γ(5, 1.5) guarantees the fault-tolerant realtime scheduling of ten tasks.

div.head: V. CONCLUSIONS
div.p: In this paper, we defined a new framework for fault-tolerant hierarchical real-time scheduling. The framework includes fault-manager module which detects faults in a component and recovers a task fault by executing its backup task in the component. In order to abstract the component fault-tolerant real-time requirement, a new interface model is provided for specifying additional resource supply in case of fault occurrence. We also analyze the fault-tolerant rate monotonic scheduling algorithm for a given periodic resource model of a component. Throughout the case study, we showed that the proposed algorithm is useful in fault-tolerant partitioning of avionics software in mission computers.
As the paper proposes a new framework for fault-tolerant hierarchical real-time scheduling, there are many issues to be solved as follows.

• Utilization bound analysis of FT-RM: The utilization bound defines the minimum resource utilization of a scheduling algorithm. We plan to derive the utilization bound of the proposed FT-RM algorithm in a periodic resource model. • Analysis of various fault-tolerant real-time scheduling algorithms: Although the scheduling analysis is based on RM, more analysis is required for various fault-tolerant real-time scheduling algorithms.

• Deriving an interface model: The interface model abstracts a component real-time requirement in a single unit to its upper-layer component. Thus, it is an important issue to compose multi-layer components in a system. We are currently working on how to derive the interface model for fault-tolerant real-time scheduling of a component. • Refinement of the framework: More refinement about the framework is required, such as fault-tolerant periodic resource model, component-level fault-tolerance, and so on. • Implementation the proposed framework: The proposed framework will be used for designing and developing safety-critical avionics mission computers. As IMA (Integrated Modular Avionics) architecture becomes popular in avionic software design, the proposed framework will enhance temporal partitioning scheme in IMA-based avionics systems.
